newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Bezeq offer may include foreign tranche.
newsitem.headline: Bezeq offer may include foreign tranche.

text.p: The government is weighing a plan to sell shares in Bezeq Israel Telecom in separate domestic and overseas tranches, sources involved in the company's privatisation said on Tuesday.

The sources said the plan was to sell shares in the Israeli capital market equal to about 10 percent of equity in the state-controlled phone company and market another block of 10 to 15 percent to foreign investors.
The shares sold to overseas investors would also be listed for trading on the Tel Aviv Stock Exchange, the sources said.
A year ago the government successfully floated shares in Israel Discount Bank using the same system.
Sources said the plan was aimed at floating the maximum possible number of shares at a time when the Israeli market is seen as too weak to absorb an offering as big as 25 percent of Bezeq.
"In order to sell 25 percent of the company they can't do it in Israel alone," said one source, who asked not to be named.
At the company's current market capitalisation, an offering of that size would be worth $460 million.

The plan, which sources stressed was still being debated, marks the latest twist in efforts by the government of Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu to further privatise Bezeq, Israel's main telecommunications carrier.

In February, Communications Minister Limor Livnat gave her support to a plan to float Bezeq shares domestically, rather than overseas as originally planned, saying a global offering could not be done before the end of 1997.
Officials said they hoped to conduct the domestic offering in July based on Bezeq's first-quarter results. Selling 25 percent of Bezeq would reduce the state's holding to 51 percent.

Sources said Bezeq still preferred to proceed with a global offering because they believe it would raise the company's profile with international investors at a time when it is seeking to borrow money in overseas financial markets.

They also would prefer an offering of new shares, whose proceeds would go to the company and enable it to repay debentures the government holds in it. The current plans call for the government to sell its Bezeq shares.
